c.tagline: Cambodia's laid-back second city, where French colonial streets meet bamboo trains and hilltop caves.

taxi.fareNote: No metered taxis; tuk-tuk and moto fares are agreed before the ride, or booked via the PassApp Taxi app

emergency.note: Emergency response outside Phnom Penh and Siem Reap can be slow; for serious issues, contact hotel/guesthouse staff and rely on travel medical evacuation insurance

avoid.reason: Motorbike bag-snatching occurs, so keep bags on the side away from the road, and stick to well-trodden paths in the surrounding countryside because of residual landmines/UXO.

hood_desc: Battambang's best-preserved stretch of French colonial shophouses and villas, lining the Sangkae River in the town center. It's the most walkable part of town, with cafes, galleries, and the starting point for bamboo train and countryside tours.

The Art Deco central market building and the streets around it form Battambang's commercial heart, packed with produce stalls, textiles, and street food. It's the busiest, most local part of the city by day.

A cluster of century-old wooden Khmer houses on stilts just south of downtown, several open to visitors as informal museums. It offers a quiet, rural counterpoint to the town center, best explored by bicycle.

A limestone hill about 12km outside town, topped by a pagoda and home to the sobering Killing Caves, a Khmer Rouge-era memorial site. Bats pour out of a nearby cave at dusk in one of the region's best-known sights.

Home to Prasat Banan, an 11th-century Angkorian-era temple atop a steep 350-step climb, often called a mini Angkor Wat. The surrounding countryside is dotted with rural villages and a small local winery.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water and skip ice of unknown origin.

transit.pay: Cash (Riel or USD); negotiate fare before riding, or book through the PassApp Taxi app
transit.map: No formal transit map; the PassApp Taxi app covers Battambang
transit.note: There is no public bus or rail network in town; tuk-tuks and motos are the primary way to get around

air: Battambang Airport (BBM) - currently no scheduled commercial flights
train: Cambodia's reactivated Phnom Penh–Poipet line passes through Battambang with very limited passenger service
bus: Frequent buses/vans from Phnom Penh (~5hr), Siem Reap (~3hr), and the Poipet border (~2.5hr)
ferry: Seasonal riverboat to Siem Reap via the Sangkae River and Tonle Sap, wet season only

tip.r: Small tips (5-10%) are appreciated at restaurants; rounding up fares for tuk-tuk and moto drivers is common
